prize_parts.citation: for empirical research showing how technology and trade shocks reshape labour demand, local labour markets and wage inequality

statement.case_for: B022 asks a first-order question: who bears the adjustment costs of technological change and import competition. It answers with unusually transparent empirical designs. The task-based account of labour demand and the China-shock evidence on local labour markets have both been widely replicated, criticised and extended since about 2003 and 2013. The discovery is therefore tested rather than merely influential. The work also bridges labour economics and trade, a link that economics has been slow to make. Attribution for the China-shock strand is clean: Autor, Dorn and Hanson jointly produced the core papers. Autor is the common thread running through the task framework as well. In my opening I proposed Katz as the third name. After reading colleagues, I now think that was the weaker choice. The citation I propose names the trade-shock and technology evidence, not the earlier skill-premium literature, so the three China-shock authors are the more defensible credited set. I did not move because of support counts. I moved because the attribution arguments hold up.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the central empirical magnitudes are still contested. These include the size and persistence of the China-shock effects, the sensitivity of shift-share designs, and the long-run labour-market consequences. The task-based theory also has contributors outside the credited set (Acemoglu, Levy, Murnane), and the 2024 prize touched adjacent themes on technology and institutions. If the Committee reads the prize as covering the task framework, it must either broaden the names or narrow the citation to the empirical evidence. The work is also less conceptually foundational than a model-based contribution such as B007 or B047, and some may see it as measurement and design rather than theory.

responses.point: Enflo ranks B022 first and proposes Autor, Hanson and Dorn. She argues the China-shock trio is the cleanest credited set and leaves Katz out because his earlier skill-biased-change work is a separate strand. She also notes that the persistence and magnitude of the trade effects remain contested.
responses.response: I agree with the attribution logic and revise my opening accordingly, replacing Katz with Dorn. Katz's skill-premium and education-technology work is foundational, but it is not the discovery this citation names. It would also leave the Committee free to recognise him elsewhere, since he appears in B014. I share her caution on magnitudes, but I would treat the dispute as evidence of a living, tested literature. The prize should reward the research design and the demonstrated adjustment costs, not any single point estimate.

responses.point: Hassler proposes only Autor and Hanson for B022. He argues that attribution is blurred between task-based theory (Acemoglu and Autor) and the empirical China-shock work, and that Dorn's role is secondary. He also notes that some persistence findings have been challenged in re-analyses.
responses.response: The blur he identifies is real, and it is why I think the citation must be framed around the empirical evidence on technology and trade shocks, not around task-model theory. Under that framing Dorn is a co-author of the core China-shock papers, so excluding him is harder to justify than including him. I accept that a two-person prize is a defensible alternative if the Committee wants to narrow it. But I would not give Hanson a place without Dorn when the credit is a joint trio. I also accept that the re-analyses are a genuine uncertainty. I would want the Scientific Background to address them directly.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B012 (Helpman and Melitz) first. He argues that firm heterogeneity is the standard foundation of modern trade analysis, with more than two decades of confirmation, and that trade has not been recognised since 2008.
responses.response: I take the merit argument seriously and keep B012 close, since the framework is very mature. My hesitation is attribution. Credit for firm-level heterogeneity is shared with Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, who are not on the ballot entry, as several colleagues note. Helpman also appears in B007, so the Committee should decide which of his bodies of work it wants to recognise. B022 has a cleaner credited set for its specific discovery. The absence of a trade prize since 2008 is a timing consideration, not scientific merit, and B022 itself spans trade and labour.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B007 fourth. He judges the Grossman–Helpman political-economy contribution clearly joint but narrower than their wider agenda, with mixed empirical support for the lobbying model.
responses.response: That is a fair qualification of my own opening first choice. The attribution to Grossman and Helpman is the cleanest on the shortlist, but the lobbying model's precise predictions have only mixed empirical support, and the contribution is narrow if framed around protection alone. Seeing how few colleagues ranked it, and weighing the argument that it is narrower than the competing candidates, I now treat B007 as an alternative rather than my lead. I keep it because the conceptual originality is high and the credit is unambiguous.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee will frame the citation around the empirical trade-shock and technology evidence, or try to include task-model theory, which would raise attribution problems outside the credited set.
How much weight the continuing re-analyses of China-shock persistence and magnitude should carry against the demonstrated adjustment-cost finding.
Whether Dorn or Katz is the better third name. I now favour Dorn for the China-shock citation, but the choice depends on how the final citation is worded.
How the 2024 prize on technology and institutions bears on timing for B022 and on distinctiveness for B047.
My attribution judgments rest on my own reading and recollection of the literature and are not independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. My profile lists co-authors and collaborators in matching, kidney exchange, refugee resettlement and school choice, and none appear among the credited names for B022, B007 or B047. The SSE affiliations shared with committee colleagues concern those colleagues, not the candidates.
